question.text: The Boolean expression $\sim(p \vee q) \vee(\sim p \wedge q)$ is equivalent to

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text {  Given, } \sim(p \vee q) \vee(\sim p \wedge q) \\ & \Rightarrow(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee(\sim p \wedge q) \text { (By De Morgan's Law) } \\ & \Rightarrow \sim p \wedge(\sim q \vee q) \text { (Distributive Law) } \\ & \Rightarrow \sim p \wedge t \text { (By complement law, where } t=\text { tautology) } \\ & \Rightarrow \sim p \text { (Identity law) }\end{aligned}$
